title: GST 113 ( UNIZIK ) : FUNCTIONS OF THE LAW
subject: GST 113

questions.question: Green asserts that our conception of law is incomplete without understanding which of the following?
questions.explanation: Green asserts that our conception of law is incomplete unless we understand what it is meant to do.

questions.question: Roscoe Pound perceives law as a social institution meant to satisfy which of the following?
questions.explanation: Roscoe Pound sees law as a social institution to satisfy social wants and demands.

questions.question: Which philosophers perceive the role of law as preservation and enlargement of freedom and liberty?
questions.explanation: Hobbes and Locke perceive the role of law to be the preservation and enlargement of freedom and liberty.

questions.question: According to Kant, the purpose of law is the adjustment of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Kant opines that the purpose of law is the adjustment of freedom of the members of the society.

questions.question: Jeremy Bentham posits that the function of law is the maximization of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Bentham posits that the function of law is the maximization of the happiness of the greatest number of members of society.

questions.question: Salmond perceives law as the gateway to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Salmond perceives law as the gateway to the administration of justice.

questions.question: How many functions of law in society did Roscoe Pound identify?
questions.explanation: Roscoe Pound identified 4 functions of law in society.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of Roscoe Pound's functions of law?
questions.explanation: Pound's functions include maintaining law and order, maintaining status quo, facilitating maximum freedom, and satisfying basic needs.

questions.question: Roscoe Pound identified which of the following as a function of law?
questions.explanation: Pound identified maintaining status quo as one of the 4 functions of law.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of Roscoe Pound's functions of law?
questions.explanation: Pound identified facilitating maximum freedom of individuals as a function of law.

questions.question: Law is considered a basic function of society as a means of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Law is considered a basic function of society as a means of social control.

questions.question: Lon Fuller asserts that the function of law is to guide which of the following?
questions.explanation: Lon Fuller asserts that the function of law is to guide human conduct.

questions.question: The absence of law is an invitation to which of the following?
questions.explanation: The absence of law is an invitation to disorder, anarchy, and chaos.

questions.question: Law serves as a means of balancing competing interests by prescribing acceptable acts and forbidding which of the following?
questions.explanation: Law prescribes acceptable acts and forbids undesirable behaviours.

questions.question: Which school of thought perceives law as an instrument of social engineering?
questions.explanation: The sociological school of thought perceives law as an instrument of social engineering.

questions.question: Without law, the society will only be a jungle paving way for which of the following?
questions.explanation: Without law, the society will be a jungle paving way for anarchy, chaos, and barbarism.

questions.question: Thomas Hobbes asserts that without order, social life would be which of the following?
questions.explanation: Thomas Hobbes asserts that without order, social life would be miserable.

questions.question: Law provides a framework of rules creating legal rights, obligations, and which of the following?
questions.explanation: Law provides a framework of rules creating legal rights, obligations, and powers.

questions.question: The definition of legal rights promotes certainty and which of the following?
questions.explanation: The definition of legal rights promotes certainty and predictability.

questions.question: It is a fundamental principle of law that where there is right, there is which of the following?
questions.explanation: It is a fundamental principle of law that where there is right, there is remedy.

questions.question: Law provides a framework for the settlement of disputes and enforcement of legal rights through which of the following?
questions.explanation: Law provides the procedure for enforcement of legal rights through the machinery of the courts.

questions.question: Town planning laws are illustrative of which function of law?
questions.explanation: Town planning laws illustrate law as a means of social change, development, and planning.

questions.question: According to the positivist school, which of the following are an important element of law?
questions.explanation: According to the positivist school of thought, sanctions are an important element of law.

questions.question: John Austin posits that the provision of sanctions compels people to act in which manner?
questions.explanation: John Austin posits that the provision of sanctions compels people to act in an acceptable manner.

questions.question: Ronald Dworkin opines that the function of law is to justify the use of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Ronald Dworkin opines that the function of law is to justify the use of coercion.

questions.question: Law can be modified to suit which of the following?
questions.explanation: Law can be modified to suit the circumstances of the society.

questions.question: The Constitution of Nigeria vests law-making power on which body?
questions.explanation: The Constitution of Nigeria vests law-making power on the legislature.

questions.question: Law establishes social institutions and sets the limit of powers exercisable by which of the following?
questions.explanation: Law establishes social institutions and sets the limit of powers exercisable by office holders.

questions.question: By establishing checks and balances, each arm of government serves as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Each arm serves as a check or a watch dog on the other.

questions.question: The regulation of human conduct is one of the basic and important functions of which of the following?
questions.explanation: The regulation of human conduct is one of the basic and important functions of law.

questions.question: Social control is a concept associated with which field?
questions.explanation: Social control is not a legal concept but a concept associated with the social sciences.

questions.question: Which scholar is attributed with describing law as a specialized form of social control?
questions.explanation: The use of the concept of social control has been attributed to Roscoe Pound.

questions.question: The term social control is used by sociologists to describe mechanisms through which society maintains which of the following?
questions.explanation: Sociologists use the term to describe mechanisms through which society maintains normative social systems.

questions.question: Formal social control is an official means of regulating human behaviour, including state and which of the following?
questions.explanation: Formal social control includes state and law.

questions.question: Informal social control includes family, religion, public opinion, morality, customs, and which of the following?
questions.explanation: Informal social control includes family, religion, public opinion, morality, customs, values etc.

questions.question: Which is the most effective formal instrument of social control?
questions.explanation: Law is one of the formal and most effective instruments of social control.

questions.question: According to Nnabue, law achieves social control by first stipulating which of the following?
questions.explanation: According to Nnabue, law achieves social control by first stipulating conditions.

questions.question: Hart opines that rules must contain restrictions on the free use of violence, theft, and which of the following?
questions.explanation: Hart opines that rules must restrict violence, theft, and deception.

questions.question: The penal technique involves the use of rules which prohibits certain unacceptable acts and provides which of the following?
questions.explanation: The penal technique prohibits unacceptable acts and provides sanctions for non-compliance.

questions.question: Which technique is used to regulate crimes in society?
questions.explanation: The penal technique is used to regulate crimes in the society.

questions.question: The penal technique serves as a means of deterrence to which of the following?
questions.explanation: It serves as a means of deterrence to future perpetrators of crimes.

questions.question: Which of the following is an alternative to the penal technique?
questions.explanation: Alternatives to the penal technique include non-intervention, warning, reciprocity, and compounding.

questions.question: The grievance remedial technique applies in which type of matters?
questions.explanation: The grievance remedial technique applies in civil matters such as contract, tort, and trust.

questions.question: The private arranging technique binds only which of the following?
questions.explanation: It binds only persons who have agreed to be bound by the relevant law.

questions.question: Under the private arranging technique, a person who contracts a marriage under the Marriage Act is forbidden from contracting a subsequent marriage under which law?
questions.explanation: A person who contracted a marriage under the Marriage Act is forbidden from contracting a subsequent marriage under customary law.

questions.question: The administrative regulatory technique is preventive in its effect and enforceable by which of the following?
questions.explanation: It is enforceable by the government without necessarily identifying a victim.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an administrative regulatory agency?
questions.explanation: The Standard Organization of Nigeria and NAFDAC are examples of regulatory agencies.

questions.question: In Salomon v Salomon, the House of Lords held that a company is distinct from which of the following?
questions.explanation: The House of Lords held that Salomon Co. Ltd was a person distinct from Mr. Salomon.

questions.question: The conferral of social benefit technique involves the use of law by government to provide which of the following?
questions.explanation: This technique involves the use of law by government to provide basic amenities like roads, schools, hospitals.

questions.question: The fiscal technique is the use of taxes and levies to regulate certain acts and to do which of the following?
questions.explanation: The fiscal technique affords governments the opportunity to raise funds for executing their numerous tasks.
